title: H2 import witness
description: What the execution actually loaded, observed at import time rather than declared. The RunSpec's execution-code closure declares which repository source bytes are eligible to take part in an execution; this document proves one execution did not step outside that namespace. The two are not the same claim and neither substitutes for the other: a closure alone cannot say what ran, and a witness alone has nothing to be measured against. Correction 5 requires the first direction — the bytes used are the bytes recorded — so the gate is containment, `observed repo-local code` in `declared authority domains`, never equality with the closure. Requiring every declared member to appear would make any run that imports less than the whole repository fail, which is every run.

authority.description: Not diagnostic. An observation carrying no authority domain fails the run closed; contrast environment_import_delta.json, which records a side effect and gates nothing.

observations.description: Every repository-local file the import system resolved, sorted by path, whatever its domain. Third-party and build objects are classified here, not filtered out at the recorder: a filter at the entrance would delete the evidence before anything judged it, and the file most worth seeing is exactly the one nobody expected to be loaded.

authority_domain.description: declared_execution_code_closure: selectable repository source under a declared root, byte identity checked against the closure member. named_execution_semantics: a member of the named execution-semantics content set, byte identity checked against that member. build_witness: a native object under the invocation's bound build directory, whose identity the build witness carries. environment_external: an ignored path outside every declared root, held by the environment axis.

bootstrap.description: Evidence that the recorder was running before the code it is meant to witness. A hook installed inside the child's main() is already too late: the child's own top-level imports resolve while the module object is being created, so an in-child hook would witness everything except the modules that decide what runs. The recorder is therefore installed by a separate entry point which then loads the child.

entry_module.description: Imported only after the recorder is installed, so its own top-level imports are witnessed.

preloaded_repo_local_paths.description: Repository-local files already in sys.modules when the recorder installed — the bootstrap's own reachable set and nothing else. Recorded rather than asserted away so the claim is checkable: the verifier bounds this list, which is what makes 'installed early enough' a measurement instead of a comment.

declared.description: The authority this witness was measured against, pinned by digest so a record cannot later be read against a different declaration.

path.description: The resolved origin, symlinks followed, relative to the repository root. A module name is not a byte identity: the same file may be imported under several names, and the same name may resolve to different files.

module_names.description: Every name this one file was bound to. Sorted, so re-import order does not move the digest.

sha256.description: Taken when the import system resolved the file, not after the run, so a file rewritten mid-execution is recorded as it was used.

authority_domains.description: A set, not a discriminated kind. Since scripts/ became a declared root the domains genuinely overlap: the named execution-semantics tooling under scripts/ is also a closure member, and both bindings apply to it. Reporting may prefer one label for readability, but admission may not depend on that precedence — a file is admitted when this set is non-empty and every binding it names agrees on the bytes. An empty set is the unbound case and fails the run closed.
